questions.stem: What does an Apache Airflow job in Fabric give a team?

options.text: A KQL database for event data
A managed Apache Airflow environment for authoring and running DAGs written in Python
A deployment pipeline with Airflow branding

questions.explanation: An Apache Airflow job hosts Airflow for you, so the team writes DAGs in Python and runs them without managing the Airflow infrastructure.

questions.stem: Airflow DAGs in a workspace are scheduled to run through the night. Which pool choice keeps them running on time?

options.text: A custom pool, which can stay on
The starter pool, which shuts down after a period with no activity
No pool; Airflow jobs don't use compute

questions.explanation: The starter pool suits development and stops when idle. Scheduled production DAGs need a custom pool that stays available.

questions.stem: In which language do you write the DAGs an Apache Airflow job runs?
questions.explanation: Airflow DAGs are Python files that define tasks and their dependencies.

questions.stem: Which two are configured in a workspace's data workflow (Apache Airflow) settings? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: The sensitivity label of every item
Whether jobs use the starter pool or a custom pool

questions.explanation: The data workflow settings choose the pool and, for a custom pool, its size and scaling. Git, labels and capacity are set elsewhere.
